card.title: VP, Supply Chain & Manufacturing Operations - Santa Clara, CA - Hybrid
card.description:
At Gigamon, our purpose is to protect the hybrid networks and data of the largest, most complex organizations on the planet. Certified as a Great Place to Work, we offer a deep observability pipeline that efficiently delivers network-derived intelligence to cloud, security, and observability tools. This helps our customers to eliminate security blind spots, optimize network traffic, and dramatically reduce tool cost and complexity, enabling them to better secure and manage their hybrid cloud infrastructure. Gigamon has served more than 4,000 customers worldwide, including over 80 percent of Fortune 100 enterprises, 9 of the 10 largest mobile network providers, and hundreds of governments and educational organizations. 
 
The VP, Supply Chain & Manufacturing Operations leads the strategy and execution of Gigamon’s global supply chain and manufacturing operations. This executive oversees planning, procurement, supplier management, manufacturing, logistics, and operational execution to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality products to customers worldwide. The role partners closely with Engineering, Quality, Finance, Sales, and Customer Support to align operational capabilities with business priorities and product growth. Through disciplined execution, risk management, and continuous improvement, this leader strengthens scalability, resilience, and customer satisfaction. 
 
What you’ll do:

* Define and execute a global supply chain and manufacturing strategy aligned with Gigamon’s business objectives, product roadmap, and customer requirements.
* Lead demand and supply planning, materials management, procurement, contract manufacturing, production scheduling, inventory optimization, order fulfillment, logistics, and distribution.
* Establish scalable operating processes, systems, metrics, and governance to improve forecast accuracy, capacity utilization, delivery performance, inventory turns, cost, and working capital.
* Develop and maintain strategic relationships with contract manufacturers, suppliers, logistics providers, and other key partners.
* Drive supplier selection, qualification, performance management, capacity planning, commercial negotiations, and continuity planning.
* Build resilience across the supply chain by identifying operational risks, developing contingency plans, and ensuring effective responses to disruptions.
* Partner with Engineering and Product teams on new product introduction, product lifecycle management, design-for-manufacturability, component strategy, and engineering change control.
* Collaborate with Quality and Engineering to establish and maintain product, supplier, and manufacturing quality standards.
* Oversee global manufacturing and fulfillment operations to ensure products are delivered on time, at the required quality level, and in accordance with customer and regulatory requirements.
* Ensure compliance across global trade, tariffs, export controls, environmental requirements, and product regulations, including country-specific certifications and regulatory approvals, in partnership with Legal, Engineering, Quality, and relevant teams.
* Manage reverse-logistics operations, including customer returns and repair; oversee return-material-authorization (RMA) processes and the performance of repair providers and other service partners.
* Lead cross-functional efforts to improve operational efficiency, reduce complexity, and optimize total cost of ownership.
* Oversee product-cost and inventory governance, including standard-cost reviews, bill-of-materials (BOM) cost changes, purchase-price variance (PPV), and excess and obsolete (E&O) inventory, in partnership with Finance.
* Establish clear performance expectations and develop a high-performing, globally distributed operations organization.
* Provide executive-level reporting, recommendations, and accountability for supply chain and manufacturing performance.

What you’ve done:

* Led global supply chain, manufacturing, and operations organizations in a technology, networking, telecommunications, electronics, or similarly complex product environment.
* Developed and executed supply chain strategies supporting global customers, multiple product lines, and evolving demand profiles.
* Managed outsourced manufacturing models, including contract manufacturer relationships, supplier networks, production capacity, and end-to-end fulfillment.
* Built expertise across demand planning, supply planning, procurement, inventory management, logistics, manufacturing operations, and supplier performance.
* Delivered measurable improvements in service levels, forecast accuracy, inventory turns, cost, quality, cycle time, or working capital.
* Led successful new product introductions and product transitions in partnership with Engineering, Product Management, Quality, and Finance.
* Implemented operating mechanisms, systems, analytics, and performance metrics that improved visibility and decision-making across the supply chain.
* Managed significant operational risk, including supplier concentration, component availability, capacity constraints, geopolitical disruption, and business continuity.
* Negotiated and managed strategic supplier and manufacturing agreements with an understanding of commercial, operational, and quality considerations.
* Built, developed, and led high-performing global teams through growth, transformation, and organizational change.
* Demonstrated experience presenting operational performance, risks, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership.
* Held a bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, operations, engineering, business, or a related discipline; an advanced degree is preferred.

Who you are:

* A strategic and hands-on operations leader who connects long-term business objectives with disciplined day-to-day execution.
* A customer-focused partner who understands how supply chain performance affects product availability, customer experience, and business growth.
* A data-driven decision-maker who uses operational metrics, financial insight, and sound judgment to prioritize action.
* A collaborative executive who builds trust across Engineering, Product, Quality, Finance, Sales, and Customer Support.
* An effective communicator who can translate complex operational issues into clear decisions, priorities, and accountability.
* A resilient and adaptable leader who anticipates risk, responds decisively to disruption, and drives continuous improvement.
* A talent developer who establishes high standards, empowers teams, and creates an inclusive environment where people can perform at their best.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

card.title: Senior Manager - Biomanufacturing, Manufacturing Technical Operations
card.description:
**About Site**
--------------

Catalent’s Madison, Wisconsin site is a state‑of‑the‑art biologics development and manufacturing facility supporting customers from research through early‑ and mid‑stage clinical production. Located at 726 Heartland Trail in Madison, the approximately 102,700‑square‑foot GMP facility specializes in mammalian cell line engineering, drug substance biomanufacturing, and biopharmaceutical development, utilizing flexible single‑use systems to enable rapid scale‑up and customization. The site is home to Catalent’s proprietary GPEx® and GPEx® Lightning technologies, which are used to generate high‑yielding mammalian cell lines for biologic therapies, and supports production scales ranging from 50 to 4,000 liters for clinical manufacturing. Following a $45 million expansion announced in 2025, the Madison site has significantly increased capacity, added new equipment, and created approximately 200 highly skilled biohealth jobs, further strengthening its role within Catalent’s global biologics network and Wisconsin’s growing life sciences ecosystem.

**Position Summary**
--------------------

We have an opportunity for a Senior Manager - Biomanufacturing, Manufacturing Technical Operations to join our team. This role leads the Manufacturing Technical Operations organization, including Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing Compliance, Deviation Investigation, and Manufacturing Training. The position ensures safe, compliant, and reliable biomanufacturing operations while driving continuous improvement and technical excellence. The successful candidate will help strengthen workforce capability, reduce operational risk, and ensure sustainable preventive solutions across manufacturing operations.

Shift: Monday - Friday 8:00AM - 5:00PM 
Location: Madison, WI 
100% Onsite

**The Role**
------------

* Lead, coach, develop, and evaluate leaders and technical professionals supporting Manufacturing Engineering, Compliance, Deviation Investigation, and Training.
* Establish clear goals, role accountabilities, performance expectations, succession plans, and development strategies for the organization.
* Provide organizational ownership for Manufacturing-based engineering support and technical response to process, equipment, materials, automation, documentation, and execution issues.
* Establish and govern a structured Rapid Response Team process that defines the problem, operational impact, containment, technical resources, decision ownership, recovery plan, communications, and escalation pathway.
* Provide leadership and oversight for Manufacturing deviation investigations, including investigation quality, aging, cycle time, right-first-time approval, and recurring-event reduction.
* Ensure investigations are fact-based and clearly distinguish event description, product and process impact, root cause, contributing factors, correction, corrective action, and preventive action.
* Establish Manufacturing Technical Operations as a key owner and contributor to process readiness, including batch production record review, dry runs, equipment readiness, material availability, qualification status, and execution-risk review.
* Ensure new equipment is transitioned into routine use with defined operational ownership, procedures, training, spare parts, maintenance, and troubleshooting strategies.
* Establish an integrated performance-management system using measures such as recurrence, recovery time, repeat failures, downtime, deviation aging, investigation right-first-time performance, corrective and preventive action aging and effectiveness, qualification progress, equipment reliability, open risks, and project delivery.
* Use performance data to establish priorities, allocate resources, escalate risk, and hold leaders accountable for outcomes.

**The Candidate**
-----------------

### **Minimum Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Biotechnology, Biological Sciences, Biochemistry, or another relevant scientific or technical discipline required.
* Ten (10) or more years of relevant manufacturing, engineering, technical operations, Manufacturing Science and Technology, Quality, or related experience.
* Five (5) or more years of progressive leadership experience, including responsibility for technical professionals, people leaders, or manufacturing-support organizations.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex technical problem solving and operational recovery in a Good Manufacturing Practice manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience with deviation investigations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, root-cause analysis, inspection readiness, and quality risk management.
* Advanced understanding of current Good Manufacturing Practice biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including upstream, downstream, solution-preparation, equipment, and support systems.
* Demonstrable leadership experience at Catalent (including but not limited to participation in Catalent‑sponsored leadership programs such as Next Generation Global Leaders, GOLD, LEAD Now, General Manager Excellence, and GROW) may be considered in place of external experience.

### **Preferred Skills & Background**

* Advanced degree preferred.
* Experience in Good Manufacturing Practice biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

**Why You Should Join Catalent**
--------------------------------

* Defined career path and annual performance review and feedback process.
* Diverse, inclusive culture.
* Potential for career growth on an expanding team within an organization dedicated to preserving and bettering lives.
* Competitive paid time off plus 8 paid holidays.
* Community engagement and green initiatives.
* Medical, dental, and vision benefits effective day one of employment.
* Tuition reimbursement.

**Catalent offers rewarding opportunities to further your career!** Join the global drug development and delivery leader and help us bring over 7,000 life-saving and life-enhancing products to patients around the world. Catalent is an exciting and growing international company where employees work directly with pharma, biopharma and consumer health companies of all sizes to advance new medicines from early development to clinical trials and to the market. Catalent produces more than 70 billion doses per year, and each one will be used by someone who is counting on us. Join us in making a difference.

card.title: Sr. Director, Global Manufacturing Strategy & Network Transformation
card.description:
Location:
Buffalo, NY, US, 14213

Req ID: 41812

Segment: Supply Chain

Rich’s, also known as Rich Products Corporation, is a family-owned food company dedicated to inspiring possibilities. From cakes and icings to pizza, appetizers and specialty toppings, our products are used in homes, restaurants and bakeries around the world. Beyond great food, our customers also gain insights to help them stay competitive, no matter their size. Our portfolio includes creative solutions geared at helping food industry professionals compete in foodservice, retail, in-store bakery, deli, and prepared foods, among others. With more than 13,500 associates working globally in 100 countries and annual sales of $5.9 billion, Rich’s is a global leader with a focus on everything that family makes possible. Rich’s®—Infinite Possibilities. One Family.

**Purpose Statement**
---------------------

The Senior Director/VP, Global Manufacturing Strategy & Network Transformation will shape and drive the long-term manufacturing strategy for the enterprise, with primary accountability for the global TCCS manufacturing network and a broader mandate to identify opportunities across the total manufacturing enterprise. Reporting to the Head of Operations, this leader will guide critical decisions around manufacturing footprint, capacity and capability, capital deployment, technology, and operating standards across businesses and regions.

This role will be instrumental in ensuring the manufacturing network is positioned to support significant global growth and evolving business needs. * Food or beverage manufacturing experience preferred; experience with aseptic, UHT, frozen, or dairy processing is a plus.
* Exposure to manufacturing performance and asset programs such as TPM, OEE and yield improvement, lean, critical spares and equipment life-cycle management, equipment standardization and sourcing, or digital and Smart Factory initiatives.
* Experience working in a global, matrixed organization with teams across regions and time zones (for example, Asia, Europe, and Latin America). Fluency in English required; additional languages a plus.

* Learns fast and drives results: a self-starter who gets up to speed quickly on new businesses, technologies, and regions, and can build a new role and strategy with minimal direction.
* Clear communicator, humble, and collaborative: communicates well up and down the organization and across cultures, follows up in writing, readily shares credit, and adapts their style to different audiences.

card.description:
**PLANT OPERATIONS CAREERS**

Plant Manager

Lead a healthcare laundry plant.

**Where** [City, ST]

**Reports to** General Manager / Regional Vice President

As Plant Manager, you'll lead the full plant (production, maintenance, quality, and logistics) with accountability for safety, budget, and the healthcare customers who depend on clean, safe linen every day.

Why you'll like it here

**Own the plant**

Daily operations, people, budget, and results.

**Lean in action**

Drive improvement with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.

**Lead leaders**

Develop supervisors, maintenance staff, and production Associates.

**Healthcare standards**

Run an operation held to OSHA and HLAC requirements.

What you'll own

* Lead and manage the Safety & Health Program within the production environment.
* Lead, motivate, and develop a team of supervisors, maintenance staff, and production associates.
* Oversee daily plant operations, including production scheduling, labor forecasting, staffing, and workflow optimization.
* Drive process improvements using Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Manage plant budget, including labor, maintenance, and operational expenses.
* Oversee inventory management to ensure consistent material supply and stock levels.

What you need

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, or Business Administration required.
* 5–7 years of leadership experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
* Strong end-to-end understanding of plant operations, including safety, quality, maintenance, and compliance.
* Proven experience managing P&L, budgeting, payroll, and cost controls.
* Strong problem-solving, analytical, and strategic thinking skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and ERP systems.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills.

**Physical requirements**

* Ability to stand, walk, and move throughout a manufacturing facility for extended periods.
* Ability to occasionally lift up-to fifty (50) pounds.
* Comfortable working in a plant/production environment.
* Ability to push and pull carts of linen regularly.
* Ability to use required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, and work boots.

**Bonus points**

* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Six Sigma methodologies preferred.
* PMP (Project Management Professional) certification.
* Willing to relocate- GOE flexibility.
* Prior military leadership experience (e.g., Sergeant or above) a plus.
* Familiarity with ISO 14001 / ISO 9001 and GMP standards.
* Experience with manufacturing systems and reporting tools

**We'll teach you:** Our plant network, operating standards, and the support of a national organization.

How we work

Every ImageFIRST Associate lives our four Core Values. These are our required competencies.

**Be Respectful**

Value all we come in contact with.

**Be Remarkable**

Create a positive moment with every interaction.

**Be Safe**

Keep ourselves and those around us safe.

**Be Honest**

Be guided by truthfulness in all we do.

Great work gets noticed

**Everyday recognition**

Coworkers nominate each other for going above and beyond, and those nominations go up in the office for everyone to see.

**All Stars & Council of Excellence**

Each year, Associates who live our values are nominated as All-Stars and earn a certificate and a cash award. Top winners join the Council of Excellence with an additional reward.

Benefits

Weekly pay

Medical, Dental, Vision

Pet, Legal, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance

401(k) with company match

Paid Time Off package

Paid Parental Leave

Tuition Reimbursement

Referral Program

Great company culture

Collaborative team environment

 

**MILITARY & VETERANS**

Served? Your skills fit here.

Officers and senior NCOs who led maintenance, logistics, or production operations: command a plant. Whether you're transitioning out, serving in the Guard or Reserve, or a veteran, we want to hear from you.

* Leading a unit leading supervisors, maintenance, and production
* Readiness and inspections safety, quality, and compliance
* Resource stewardship plant budget and cost control

Guard and Reserve members: we support your service commitments. Tell us your branch and specialty when you apply.

 

Who we are

ImageFIRST is the nation's largest medical-focused linen and laundry provider, serving health systems, hospitals, and outpatient facilities since 1967. We run more HLAC-accredited facilities than anyone else, and 97% of our customers stay with us.

Our mission: improving the lives of our associates, our customers, and the patients they serve.

**If you're ready to own a plant's results, apply today.**

 

**Equal Opportunity Employer / Drug-Free Workplace**

We maintain a drug-free workplace in compliance with state and federal law. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are fueled by the talent, passion, and diversity of our associates.

card.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

**Position Summary**

CVS is seeking a Senior Manager to own the end-to-end process and technology strategy for stocking and picking across CVS Distribution. This role sits within the Operational Excellence (OpEx) Initiatives team, reporting to the Executive Director of Operational Excellence Initiatives (whose peers lead the OpEx Regional and OpEx Analytics organizations), alongside three other Senior Managers and a team of Managers/Senior Analysts. This role has two direct reports. Where peer Senior Managers on the team own the inbound-through-machine-replenishment and inbound/outbound value streams, this role owns the network's stocking and picking processes – the highest-volume and most labor-intensive processes in our network. This individual will also serve as the process-side subject matter expert on Warehouse Management System (WMS) configuration within owned value streams, to ensure system and process are in alignment. The role requires approximately 30–50% travel, often in stretches on an every-other-week cadence.

Responsibilities:

* **Technology Deployment (50%) —** Own the 3-year technology roadmap for stocking, picking, and module support, including code updates to existing processes, new process rollouts, and major enhancements, to improve colleague experience, quality, and productivity.
* + **Success Measures** — Deliver measurable improvements in inventory accuracy, stocking and picking quality defects, and throughput, specific to each enhancement or process change.
* **Process Optimization (15%) —** Own the process and technology, and advise on WMS configuration needs within your value streams, working with the other subject matter experts on the team who consult on and implement WMS changes, to tune system settings, improve operations, and keep WMS, technology, and process aligned across stocking and picking:
* + **Stocking —** Own the process and core technology for replenishing split-case picking modules
* + **Picking —** Own the process and core technology for picking across multiple picking methods, including split case and full case, in both active pick slots and reserve storage locations
* **Project & Change Management (25%) —** Plan and execute multiple concurrent projects (typically 4–5 programs in parallel, with a rollout roughly every other week across approximately 2,000 associates), applying strong project management skills — managing risk, critical path, dependencies, and budget — to meet project goals on time. Larger programs are led by the network Center of Excellence (COE); on others, this role provides oversight while the site leads. Build the financial business case and project plan for new opportunities, and ensure robust follow-through on changes to sustain results.
* **Mentorship/Training (10%)—** Grow and shape the organization's lean capability, developing training content and standard work that enhances the continuous improvement culture across the network. Lead, coach, and develop direct reports.

This is a work-from-home role with travel; relocation is not offered. The ideal candidate is located near one of the following distribution centers: La Habra (CA), Patterson (CA), Conroe (TX), Lumberton (NJ), Woonsocket (RI), Chemung (NY), Novi (DT), Kansas City (MO), Indianapolis (IN), Orlando (FL), North Augusta (SC), Fredericksburg (VA), or Knoxville (TN).

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related engineering/science field or additional 4 years of experience in the requirements below
* 6+ years' experience in a manufacturing or distribution center environment
* 4+ years of demonstrated success and experience in Lean Manufacturing, Continuous Improvement, or Operational Excellence in a manufacturing or warehouse operation
* 4+ years of demonstrated success in managing projects
* 4+ years of experience with WMS, ERP, MES, or LMS systems and database structure

* 2+ years of experience with SQL
* Proven ability to influence and partner with operations, IT, and finance leaders; strong written and verbal communication; self-motivated and effective at managing multiple priorities 
 
 **Preferred Qualifications**
* 9+ years' experience in a manufacturing or distribution center environment
* 6+ years as continuous improvement, industrial engineering, or process engineering
* 2+ years of experience with Microsoft Azure Snowflake semantic modeling and Power BI
* 2+ years running operations (plant manager, senior operations manager, etc.)
* Certified in standards-based time and motion study systems such as MOST and MTM
* APICS CPIM, CSCP, or CLTD Certified
* PMP Certified
* Six Sigma Black Belt Certified

**Pay Range**

The typical pay range for this role is:

$82,940.00 - $182,549.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.

**Great benefits for great people**

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

 
This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility.

Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments.

 
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on: 12/14/2026

Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with all federal, state and local laws.

card.title: Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch
card.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.

With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.

**LOCATION:** Remote with Travel

US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.

This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.

The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. This person establishes the PMO, sets objective gate criteria and metrics, holds functional leaders and partners accountable without direct authority, challenges unrealistic plans, and leads recovery when programs fall behind. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

***Quality Management and Launch Readiness Across Supply Chain Partners***

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive post-launch stabilization, ensuring yield, quality, and delivery targets are met before handoff to steady-state operations.

***Advanced Manufacturing and Capacity***

* Identify and drive advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and technologies needed to meet critical customer demand and scale production.
* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.
* Partner with equipment providers, consultants, and IDEX sites to accelerate process development and transfer best practices.
* Champion design for manufacturability, lean, and continuous improvement in all new product introductions.
* Ensure process qualification, fixtures, tooling, controls, operator readiness, capacity, and rate trials are incorporated before design freeze and production release.

***Metrics, Visibility, and Results***

* Define and own program and launch KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that provide clear leadership visibility across BUs and partners.
* Identify risks early—schedule, resource, quality, sourcing, cost, capacity, and production readiness—and drive countermeasures and recovery plans.
* Challenge unrealistic timelines, resource assumptions, and commitments; escalate decisions and support needs to executive leadership.
* Deliver regular executive updates on portfolio status, risks, decisions, and results.
* Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support program execution, supplier engagement, site coordination, customer needs, and equipment-provider activities.
* Perform other related duties and support additional program, PMO, or business needs as assigned.

**KEY PERFORMANCE METRICS:**

* On-time milestone and launch attainment across the NPD portfolio.
* PPAP on-time completion and first-pass approval rate across internal sites, sister BUs, and supply chain partners.
* PFMEA, DFMEA, and control plan completion prior to required gates.
* Launch quality, including first-pass yield, PPM, and escapes at launch and 90 days post-launch.
* Ramp-to-rate performance, including time to target capacity and on-time delivery to customers.
* Critical manufacturing process readiness, including qualification and demonstrated capability for welding/joining, filtration manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test as applicable.
* Program budget, Capex, and product cost performance versus business case.
* Supplier and partner quality and delivery performance on launch programs.
* New product and IDEX-connected growth revenue enabled.
* PMO team capability, staffing, and retention.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Proven leader who has built and scaled a PMO, NPD launch, or program management function in a manufacturing environment.
* undefined
* Deep experience with APQP and product launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, and production part qualification.
* Track record driving quality and launch execution across multiple supply chain partners, contract manufacturers, and internal sites.
* Experience identifying and implementing advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and capacity expansions to meet demanding customer ramps.
* undefined
* Demonstrated success leading across multiple business units in a matrixed organization; multi-BU or IDEX experience preferred.
* Strong business acumen in make-versus-buy, multi-site manufacturing, CapEx, tooling, cost, capacity, and risk decisions.
* Builds metrics, dashboards, and operating cadence that drive accountability and measurable results.
* Influential leader able to align executives, BU partners, and suppliers, and hold owners accountable without direct authority.
* Strong executive communicator who turns complex program information into clear decisions and actions.
* Experience with welding/joining, filtration, pneumatics, fluid handling, pumps, compressors, blowers, valves, electromechanical products, precision manufacturing, data center, thermal management, or engineered industrial components preferred.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or PMP certification preferred; working knowledge of the IDEX Operating Model and 80/20 a plus.
* Proficient with project management tools, dashboards, and Microsoft Office applications.

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of program management, NPD, manufacturing launch, quality, or operations experience, including 5+ years leading teams, with experience in industrialization, supplier development, site transfers, and multi-site manufacturing.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

* While performing the duties of the job, the employee is required to move around and be still, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear.
* Employee will occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.
* Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

**Entity:** CSL Behring

**Job Category:** Research Development & Sciences

**Job Family:** Clinical Development Operations

**Job Type:** Full Time

**Location****:** King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, United States

**Employer Reference:** R-296735

**Job Description**
-------------------

**Senior Director, Performance Management & Continuous Improvement**
====================================================================

 
 

**Location: King of Prussia, PA or Melbourne, Australia | Hybrid – 3 days onsite**
==================================================================================

 
 

CSL Behring is a global biopharmaceutical leader committed to developing innovative therapies for patients with rare and serious diseases. Through scientific innovation, operational excellence, and a deep commitment to patients, we strive to transform treatment options and address significant unmet medical needs.

 
 

**The Opportunit****y**
=======================

 
 

The Senior Director, Performance Management & Continuous Improvement will provide strategic leadership for an integrated R&D capability focused on strengthening organizational performance, accelerating execution, and maximizing the value of R&D investment.

 
 

This is a high-impact leadership role that connects performance analytics, continuous improvement, program execution, and organizational change to help transform how R&D operates. The successful candidate will establish a strategic vision for how performance insights translate into meaningful business action, enabling leadership to identify opportunities, optimize resources, prioritize investments, and drive sustainable improvements across the global R&D organization.

 
 

Leading a multidisciplinary team, the Senior Director will oversee a portfolio of interconnected capabilities, including performance metrics and analytics, continuous improvement, major R&D initiatives, change management, process management, and project management tools and capability development.

This individual will serve as a strategic partner to R&D leadership, bringing together data, people, and processes to strengthen decision-making, improve operational effectiveness, and build a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

 
 

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

 
 

**R&D Performance Management & Resource Optimization**
======================================================

 
 

* Establish and evolve an integrated performance management framework for R&D, including objectives, KPIs, benchmarks, and operational performance measures.
* Lead the development of resource capacity and schedule management strategies aligned with portfolio priorities, governance, and delivery commitments.
* Leverage performance data and analytics to identify trends, opportunities, risks, and areas requiring intervention.
 

 

**Executive Insights & Strategic Decision Support**
===================================================

 
 

* Translate complex performance data into meaningful insights, recommendations, and executive-level reporting.
* Partner with senior R&D leaders to support strategic decision-making, resource optimization, investment prioritization, and organizational effectiveness.
* Establish a consistent approach to performance reviews and business insights that drives accountability and informed action.
 

 

**Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence**
===================================================

 
 

* Define and lead the continuous improvement strategy across R&D, identifying opportunities to increase productivity, improve processes, reduce costs, and enhance organizational effectiveness.
* Prioritize improvement initiatives based on strategic value, business impact, and alignment with R&D objectives.
* Drive structured problem-solving and data-driven improvement methodologies to ensure sustainable outcomes and measurable benefits.
* Establish governance, sponsorship, and performance measures to track the success and long-term impact of improvement initiatives.
 

 

**Strategic Initiatives & Cross-Functional Execution**
======================================================

 
 

* Provide portfolio-level leadership and oversight for major, cross-functional R&D initiatives.
* Ensure initiatives are aligned with strategic priorities and supported by disciplined planning, governance, stakeholder engagement, and transparent reporting.
* Coordinate improvement initiatives across R&D functions, ensuring teams move effectively from identifying business challenges to implementing sustainable solutions.
* Proactively identify barriers, manage escalations, and maintain focus on execution and measurable outcomes.
 

 

**Enterprise Change Management & Transformation**
=================================================

 
 

* Lead the development and execution of change management strategies supporting the adoption of new processes, systems, governance models, and ways of working across R&D.
* Ensure initiatives have comprehensive change plans, including stakeholder assessments, communications, training, sponsorship, change networks, readiness assessments, and adoption measures.
* Partner with Quality and other relevant functions to ensure changes within GxP-regulated environments meet applicable SOP, training, documentation, and inspection-readiness requirements.
* Drive organizational alignment and adoption to ensure transformation initiatives deliver lasting business value.
 

 

**Process Management & Organizational Learning**
================================================

 
 

* Strengthen R&D process effectiveness through structured issue resolution, process reviews, audit implementation, and continuous improvement practices.
* Promote consistent use of Before- and After-Action Reviews to capture lessons learned and improve future execution.
* Establish mechanisms to share best practices and embed organizational learning across R&D.
 

 

**Project Management Capability & Development**
===============================================

 
 

* Provide strategic direction for common project management tools, methodologies, templates, and governance practices.
* Sponsor project management capability-building initiatives, including PM Academy activities, to strengthen execution and delivery discipline across R&D.
* Promote consistent project management practices that enable teams to effectively plan, manage, and deliver complex initiatives.
 

 

**People Leadership & Organizational Integration**
==================================================

 
 

* Lead, develop, and inspire a multidisciplinary performance management and continuous improvement team.
* Establish a clear vision, priorities, and accountabilities across performance analytics, continuous improvement, major initiatives, change management, and project management capabilities.
* Foster collaboration and integration across disciplines, coach and develop talent, and create an environment focused on innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
 

 
 

**Qualifications & Experience**
===============================

 
 

* Bachelor's degree in Science, Business, Operations, Analytics, or a related discipline required. Master's degree in a relevant field preferred.
* Professional certifications or training in project management, Lean/Six Sigma, operational excellence, change management (Prosci, ACMP/CCMP), analytics, or related disciplines are advantageous.
* 12+ years experience in R&D operations, performance management, operational excellence, continuous improvement, strategic initiative management, program/project management, or a related discipline.
* Demonstrated success integrating performance analytics and business insights with strategic decision-making and practical improvement execution.
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities, including experience with KPIs, performance metrics, benchmarking, portfolio data, and resource management.
* Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives within a global, matrixed organization.
* Extensive experience in continuous improvement, structured problem-solving, organizational transformation, and benefits realization.
* Demonstrated expertise in enterprise change management, including stakeholder engagement, change strategy, communications, training, adoption, and resistance management.
* Strong understanding of pharmaceutical R&D and the broader research, development, and manufacturing environment.
* Proven ability to build relationships, align diverse stakeholders, and drive results across functions and geographies.
* Successful track record leading and developing multidisciplinary teams and integrating complementary capabilities into a cohesive operating model.
 

 

#LI-HYBRID

**About CSL Behring**
---------------------

CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients' needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.

CSL Behring operates one of the world's largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.

To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/.

**Our Benefits**
----------------

For more information on CSL benefits visit How CSL Supports Your Well-being | CSL.

**You Belong at CSL**
---------------------

At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future.

To learn more about inclusion and belonging visit https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging

------------------------------

CSL is an Equal Opportunity Employer. If you are an individual with a disability and need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application process, please visit https://www.csl.com/accessibility-statement.

Who we are? As the world's largest organization of board-certified pathologists and leading provider of laboratory accreditation and proficiency testing programs, the College of American Pathologists (CAP) serves patients, pathologists, and the public by fostering and advocating excellence in the practice of pathology and laboratory medicine worldwide.
 
 
Our Culture
 

* CAP employees make a meaningful difference by partnering with colleagues customers and members on challenging and rewarding work
* CAP provides its employees with an energetic and collaborative work environment and encourage opportunities to further develop their skills—offering reimbursement for educational programs and participation in events that enhance your skills
* We offer a generous compensation and benefits package, 401K, and more -- visit Careers at the CAP for more details

Brief Description
 
The Director, Supply Chain Continuous Improvement is accountable for optimizing the end-to-end flow of work across the Supply Chain & Logistics function, including order management, procurement, planning, fulfillment, distribution, and logistics, from order receipt through customer delivery. The role streamlines and simplifies work, establishes process ownership and decision rights, clarifies roles and responsibilities, designs reliable handovers, and improves on-time delivery and temperature integrity through data, cross-functional leadership, and employee coaching.
 
 
Specific Duties
 

* Provides enterprise-wide matrix leadership to process owners, functional leaders, operations managers, and cross-functional transformation teams.
* Establishes accountability for outcomes, milestones, financial benefits, risk mitigation, and sustainment across a portfolio of strategic initiatives.
* Coaches senior leaders, managers, professional staff, and frontline employees in Lean, Lean Six Sigma, structured problem solving, change leadership, and daily management.
* May lead direct reports, contractors, consultants, or dedicated project resources as the transformation portfolio evolves.
* Develop and execute a multi-year Supply Chain & Logistics continuous improvement and operational excellence strategy aligned with enterprise customer, financial, quality, and service objectives.
* Own the Supply Chain & Logistics transformation portfolio: identify opportunities, size value, prioritize initiatives, define resource requirements, and govern delivery to scope, schedule, budget, risk, and targeted benefits.
* Lead end-to-end supply chain value-stream redesign across order management, procurement, planning, fulfillment, distribution, logistics, customer service, quality, and enabling functions.
* Establish process ownership, decision rights, escalation paths, governance forums, RACI frameworks, standard work, controls, and reliable handovers.
* Create an enterprise performance-management system and single source of truth for OTIF, temperature excursions, productivity, cost, handover defects, and customer-impact measures.
* Build executive-ready business cases for process, automation, analytics, and technology investments; partner with Finance to validate baselines, track realized value, and prevent benefit leakage.
* Lead complex Lean, A3, kaizen, root-cause analysis, and problem-solving initiatives that resolve systemic constraints and deliver sustained results.
* Sponsor digital process improvement using D365, WMS, TMS, workflow automation, Power BI/Tableau, and other enterprise platforms where appropriate.
* Build organizational capability through leader standard work, training, coaching, certification pathways, communities of practice, and succession development.
* Lead change-management and stakeholder-engagement plans that drive adoption, accountability, and sustained behavioral change.
* Partner with Quality, Customer Service, Supply Chain, IT, Finance, Human Resources, cold-packaging teams, suppliers, technology partners, and external carriers.
* Present portfolio performance, financial impact, risks, decisions, and recommendations to executive leadership and governance forums.

Source of Supervision
 
The Director, Supply Chain Continuous Improvement is a seasoned supply chain and operations excellence leader accountable for creating measurable enterprise value by improving the end-to-end flow of work across Supply Chain & Logistics and the broader value chain, from order receipt through customer delivery. This role owns the continuous improvement operating system and process governance for Supply Chain & Logistics, while leading a portfolio of high-impact cross-functional initiatives that improve customer experience, service reliability, quality, temperature integrity, productivity, working capital, and cost. The Director partners with executive and functional leaders to translate supply chain and logistics strategy into scalable processes, clear decision rights, disciplined execution, and sustained financial and operational results.
 
 
Education / Experience
 

* Expert-level knowledge and practitioner of Lean, operational excellence, supply chain value-stream management, process governance, and structured problem solving.
* Demonstrated record of leading supply chain, logistics, or enterprise-scale transformations and delivering measurable improvements in customer service, quality, productivity, cycle time, cost, working capital, and operational resilience.
* Strong financial acumen, including business-case development, investment prioritization, benefit validation, sensitivity analysis, and executive-level performance reporting.
* Advanced analytical capability using data modeling, dashboards, Excel, Power BI, Tableau, or comparable tools to convert complex data into decisions and action.
* Proven ability to influence executives and functional leaders without direct authority in a complex, matrixed, and regulated environment.
* Exceptional executive communication, facilitation, negotiation, change leadership, and stakeholder-management skills.
* Preferred: Experience with D365, WMS, TMS, workflow automation, process mining, and regulated, laboratory, life-sciences, healthcare, pharmaceutical, diagnostics-distribution, or cold-chain operations.
* Bachelor's degree in Operations, Industrial or Systems Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field required; master's degree, MBA, or equivalent advanced education preferred.
* Twelve or more years of progressive experience in operational excellence, process transformation, and continuous improvement.
* Seven or more years leading teams, enterprise programs, or complex cross-functional transformation portfolios with executive visibility and measurable financial and operational outcomes.
* Experience partnering with Finance to validate benefits and with IT to deliver process-enabled digital transformation strongly preferred.
* Experience in laboratory, life sciences, healthcare, pharmaceutical, diagnostics distribution, cold chain, or another quality-driven and regulated environment preferred.

Additional Criteria
 
This position requires candidates to live within 75-miles of Northfield, IL and meet in office requirements.
 
**Salary:** $138,000 - $176,000

card.description:
**Plant Manager**
-----------------

**Lithium-Ion Battery Cell Manufacturing** 
**Packet Digital | Fargo, North Dakota | Full-Time | On-Site**

### **Help Build and Scale the Future of Battery Manufacturing**

Packet Digital is seeking an experienced **Plant Manager** to lead our lithium-ion battery cell manufacturing operations in Fargo, North Dakota.This is more than a traditional plant leadership role. We're looking for someone who knows how to **build, stabilize, and scale manufacturing operations**.As Plant Manager, you'll lead the transition from equipment commissioning and early production into stable, repeatable, higher-volume manufacturing. You'll have direct leadership responsibility for **Production, Manufacturing Engineering, and Maintenance**, while partnering closely with Quality, Accounting, IT, and other teams to increase production readiness, improve yield, strengthen equipment reliability, and build the operating systems needed for long-term growth.If you're a hands-on manufacturing leader who enjoys solving difficult production problems, developing teams, and building operations rather than simply maintaining them, this could be an exciting opportunity.

### **What You'll Own**

**ProductionFactory Ramp-Up**

* Lead daily lithium-ion battery cell manufacturing operations.
* Drive the facility's transition from commissioning and pilot production toward stable, higher-volume manufacturing.
* Develop production plans covering staffing, shifts, equipment utilization, capacity, and output.
* Establish strong daily operating rhythms through production meetings, visual management, KPI dashboards, shift accountability, escalation processes, yield reviews, corrective actions, and standard work.
* Partner with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality to improve process consistency, reduce scrap, and increase cell yield.

**Plant Performance**You'll be accountable for results across key manufacturing measures, including:

* Safety
* Cell yield and first-pass yield
* Scrap
* Overall Equipment Effectiveness and equipment availability
* Production attainment
* Schedule adherence
* Labor productivity
* Downtime
* Cost per cell
* Customer quality
* Capacity ramp

**Manufacturing Engineering**

* Lead the Manufacturing Engineering team supporting process development, equipment integration, process qualification, and production readiness.
* Prioritize engineering resources around production, quality, yield, and capacity needs.
* Oversee engineering trials, process validation, equipment modifications, and manufacturing improvements.
* Ensure new and improved processes successfully transition into routine production.

**MaintenanceEquipment Reliability**

* Lead plant maintenance strategy and preventive maintenance programs.
* Reduce unplanned downtime through effective troubleshooting and root-cause problem solving.
* Coordinate equipment commissioning and performance improvements with engineering teams and equipment suppliers.
* Monitor equipment availability, spare parts, maintenance costs, and repair activities.

**SafetyPlant Operations**

* Establish and reinforce safe operations around chemical handling, electrolyte, dry-room operations, combustible materials and dust, hazardous-energy control/LOTO, emergency response, fire protection, employee training, and environmental compliance.
* Oversee critical facility infrastructure including dry rooms, HVAC, air handling and dehumidification systems, chillers, compressed air, and other plant utilities.
* Build a manufacturing culture centered on **safety, quality, accountability, urgency, continuous improvement, and teamwork**.

### **Build the Team, Not Just the Process**

The Plant Manager will also play a major role in developing the organization around the factory.That includes workforce planning, hiring, organization design, supervisor development, operator qualification, succession planning, performance management, and shift leadership.We're looking for a leader who is equally comfortable reviewing production KPIs, troubleshooting equipment and process constraints, developing frontline leaders, and making decisions on the manufacturing floor.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a related technical field. Equivalent manufacturing leadership experience may be considered.
* **8–10+ years of manufacturing operations experience**, including **3–5+ years in plant management, operations management, or senior production leadership**.
* Experience managing production teams and maintenance operations in an industrial manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience **starting up, commissioning, or ramping new manufacturing facilities or production lines**.
* Experience with production equipment, facility infrastructure, maintenance programs, operating budgets, and manufacturing productivity.
* Experience in **lithium-ion battery manufacturing, advanced materials, electronics, automotive, aerospace, or another process-intensive manufacturing environment** is strongly preferred.

### **You'll Stand Out If You Bring**

* Experience improving manufacturing yield and reducing scrap.
* Strong knowledge of production planning, equipment reliability, and process control.
* Experience identifying manufacturing bottlenecks and translating data into corrective action.
* Experience reducing downtime and controlling manufacturing costs.
* Familiarity with **MES, ERP, production reporting, and continuous improvement methodologies**.
* A hands-on leadership style and the ability to make sound operational decisions in a fast-moving manufacturing environment.

**Why This Role Is Different**
------------------------------

This opportunity is ideal for someone who wants to **build a manufacturing operation, not simply inherit one**.You'll have the opportunity to shape how the plant operates as production scales, including its manufacturing systems, leadership structure, workforce, production discipline, maintenance strategy, engineering priorities, and continuous improvement culture. The ultimate challenge is straightforward: help turn an emerging production operation into a **safe, reliable, scalable, high-performance manufacturing facility**.

### **LocationWork Environment**

**Location:** Fargo, North Dakota 
**Work Environment:** On-Site Manufacturing FacilityThe position requires regular presence on the manufacturing floor and interaction with production, maintenance, and technical teams. Extended hours, weekends, or availability outside normal business hours may occasionally be needed to support plant operations. card.description:
The **Director of Operations** - Production Kitchen provides strategic and hands-on leadership for Taher's Plymouth, MN manufacturing operation. This role is responsible for leading safe, efficient, high-quality, and cost-effective production across food manufacturing, meal assembly, packaging, warehousing, logistics coordination, maintenance partnership, food safety, and continuous improvement.

This leader will help position the Production Kitchen for growth by strengthening operating discipline, improving production flow, developing leaders, supporting audit readiness, and ensuring Taher delivers consistent, chef-driven products that meet customer, regulatory, and company expectations.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Operational Leadership**

* Lead daily operations for Taher's Plymouth Production Kitchen, including production, packaging, warehousing, and cross-functional manufacturing support.
* Ensure safety, food quality, service, production attainment, labor efficiency, and cost expectations are met consistently.

* Develop and execute operational plans aligned with company growth and financial objectives.
* Establish clear performance expectations, operating rhythms, and accountability throughout the operations organization.

Partner with the VP of Operations

* - Manufacturing, Plant Manager, FSQA, culinary, purchasing, finance, HR, and logistics teams to align priorities and remove barriers.

**Manufacturing and Production**

* Oversee high-volume food production, meal assembly, sandwich production, packaging, and related manufacturing activities.

* Monitor production performance and implement improvements in labor efficiency, throughput, yield, downtime, and capacity utilization.

* Ensure production schedules are achieved while maintaining food safety, allergen control, product quality, labeling accuracy, and customer specifications.

* Identify and resolve operational bottlenecks and constraints.
* Lead efforts to improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) and manufacturing performance.

**Food Safety and Quality**

* Promote and maintain a strong food safety and quality culture throughout the organization.
* Ensure compliance with applicable food safety, regulatory, customer, and company requirements.

* Partner with FSQA leadership to maintain audit readiness and compliance with HACCP, GMP, SQF, FDA, USDA, allergen, environmental monitoring, sanitation, and documentation requirements.

* Support investigations and corrective actions related to food safety, quality, customer complaints, and production issues.
* Ensure operational teams understand and consistently follow food safety and quality procedures.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, productivity, cost reduction, and service.
* Apply Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and other improvement methodologies as appropriate.
* Develop and monitor key performance indicators and use data to drive decision-making.
* Reduce waste, improve yields, minimize downtime, and increase manufacturing efficiency.
* Implement standardized operating procedures and best practices across facilities.

**Maintenance and Engineering**

* Partner with maintenance and engineering teams to improve equipment reliability and reduce unplanned downtime.
* Support preventive and predictive maintenance programs.
* Participate in capital planning and prioritize investments that improve safety, capacity, quality, and operational performance.
* Lead or support equipment, automation, and facility improvement projects.

**Supply Chain and Customer Service**

* Partner with Supply Chain, Planning, Procurement, and Logistics teams to ensure efficient flow of materials and finished goods.
* Support production planning and inventory management to optimize customer service and working capital.
* Improve communication and coordination between operations and commercial teams.
* Ensure operational readiness for new products, customer requirements, and business growth.

**Financial Performance**

* Manage operational budgets and support the development of annual operating plans.
* Identify and execute cost savings and margin improvement initiatives.
* Monitor labor, materials, overhead, waste, and other key operational costs.
* Support capital investment decisions and ensure projects deliver expected business results.
* Drive operational performance that supports revenue growth and profitability.

**People Leadership**

* Lead, coach, and develop production managers, supervisors, line leads, machine operators, warehouse associates, maintenance partners, and other operational team members.
* Build a culture of accountability, teamwork, food safety discipline, urgency, employee engagement, and continuous improvement.

* Establish succession and development plans for key operations positions.
* Promote effective communication across shifts, departments, and locations.
* Ensure appropriate staffing and organizational capability to meet business objectives.

**Benefits**

* Medical & Dental
* Doctegrity Telemedical
* 401k
* Sick Time
* Vacation Time
* Lifemart Corporate Discount program
* Bonus structure
* Free turkey for Thanksgiving

Taher, Inc. is a family-owned and operated, chef-driven, food service management company. We specialize in providing K-12 school lunch management, campus dining, senior dining, catering, vending, and office beverage services to clients in our growing nationwide footprint.

Customers choose Taher for its chef-developed recipes created from natural and sustainable local sources, and for delivering the latest in culinary trends and operational resources to provide outstanding food options for our guests. Taher maintains a consistent presence in Food Service Management's Top 25 companies.

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Food Science, Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience will be considered.
8* -12+ years of progressive operations, food manufacturing, production, logistics, or plant leadership experience.
* Experience in food manufacturing, ready-to-eat foods, bakery, commissary, packaged goods, meal assembly, or high-volume production strongly preferred.

* Experience leading manufacturing operations in a high-volume, fast-paced production environment.
* Demonstrated success improving productivity, quality, service, and manufacturing costs.
* Strong knowledge of food safety, quality systems, HACCP, GMP, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, OEE, and operational performance management.
* Strong financial and business acumen.
* Proven leadership, coaching, communication, and problem-solving skills.
* Multi-site operations experience preferred.

**Core Competencies**

* Operational leadership and execution
* Manufacturing excellence
* Food safety and quality focus
* Continuous improvement
* Financial and business acumen

* Problem-solving and root-cause analysis
* Team leadership and talent development

card.description:
Description:

The Plant Manager is responsible for all Operations employees within the facility. The Plant Manager is also responsible for managing all tasks related to the maintenance of the building. The Plant Manager distributes and monitors the workload within the Operations areas, while maintaining the highest level of quality and productivity possible. The Plant Manager will make sure that all instructions are thoroughly followed, and that accurate documentation is recorded correctly for all work produced. This role will demonstrate highly effective and advanced time management, organizational and planning capabilities, strong attention to efficiency and provide exceptional internal and external customer satisfaction.

Requirements:

Other duties may be assigned as needed.

* Read, interpret, and understand the work order completely and plan work to ensure meeting of customer specifications, including reviewing materials that operators are going to use for as specified on the work order.
* Distribute work to each machine with a focus on how long it should take the operator to complete the assigned work and with a focus on what work is a priority.
* Ensure completion of jobs in a timely manner, meeting quantity requirements and maintaining a high degree of quality in all work performed.
* Effectively communicate status of equipment and work in process to VP-Operations.
* Check daily reports to ensure that reprints are being completed in a timely manner and that work orders are being closed in a timely manner.
* Check daily reports to ensure that all postage receipts are done completely and in a timely manner.
* Run end of shift reports with the use of Clarity and OPALS.
* Work with vendors to maintain equipment regarding preventive maintenance and down machines.
* Make recommendations to improve workflow, quality, efficiency, and safety: in turn reducing operating problems and improving product quality within the manufacturing area.
* Enforce all safety rules are being followed during the operation, maintenance, set-up, changing parts, or any other activity taking place.
* Enforce that no employee ever removes, disables, or otherwise tampers with the function of any safety devices installed on company property or equipment. Notify management immediately if you suspect any safety device to be malfunctioning, broken, or missing.
* Keep accurate records of work performed and materials used in accordance with Content Critical Solutions procedures.
* Enforce the return of all tools and accessories used to their proper location clean and in good condition.
* Enforce that all employees maintain a neat and orderly area. Assist in general housekeeping in common areas.
* Treat coworkers with respect and courtesy.
* Perform all reasonable requests from upper management.
* Read, understand, and comply with all written work instructions.
* Work as a team and participate in Content Critical Solutions efforts to ensure continuous improvement of processes, methodologies, productivity, and quality while reducing costs.
* Manage all tasks related to the maintenance of the building.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* This job has management responsibilities over all Operations employees in the facility.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Able to understand written and verbal instructions in English.
* Able to handle a rapidly paced work environment.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**

* High School diploma or GED.
* Prior experience working in direct mail manufacturing preferred but not required.
* Prior experience managing a facility preferred but not required.
* Knowledgeable in Microsoft Office Suite.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS**

* Ability to read and comprehend instructions, correspondences, and memos.
* Ability to verbally communicate effectively with coworkers and upper management.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS**

* Ability to perform simple addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
